title: The public event atlas: what is on, where, and who listed it
organisation: Quandamooka Country Events Engine, and through it the listing sources it names
about: Publicly listed island events, read from a local checkout of the events engine. The source publishes its own last search date and its own draft flag, and both are carried through rather than replaced with a judgement of ours. Cultural events are carried as date, place and listing source only, and are flagged for a human.

source_statement.quote: Draft event atlas. Confirm dates, permissions and contacts with the responsible source before use.

source_boundary.quote: This site is not an official permission, cultural authority, council permit, safety approval or live emergency source. It helps organisers ask clearer questions before they approach the right authority.

sync.publication_boundary: quandamooka-country-events-engine/docs/PUBLIC_BOUNDARY.md is treated as blocking by this connector. Its keep-private list includes sensitive cultural material, protected places, unapproved images or names, and incident details that identify people. None of that enters through here, whatever the data file happens to contain.

cadence.every: weekly, and always before a wave that touches the calendar
cadence.run_by: a person, after pulling that repository
cadence.reason: The git history of that repository carries repeated public source refreshes, roughly weekly through June and July 2026. A local checkout lags the remote, so a sync that did not record which commit it read would claim a currency it does not have.

confidence_scale.high: Not reachable while the source calls itself a draft, and it does. Nothing in this feed is high.
confidence_scale.medium: A listing source states this event, this date and this place, and the record quotes the atlas line.
confidence_scale.low: Not used. An event that cannot be cited is not carried.

freshness_rule: An event listing is only as true as the last public search behind it. The source names that date and this feed carries it, so a panel showing an event can show when somebody last looked rather than implying it knows what is on tonight.

wanted.what: A pull of the source repository before every sync.
wanted.why_it_matters: The checkout read here is 38 day(s) old. That repository refreshes its public event sources roughly weekly, so a stale checkout produces a stale calendar that looks current.
wanted.who_would_have_to_agree: Nobody. It is one git pull, and this connector reports the age every run.
wanted.how_small_it_could_start: It already does. This entry exists so the number is on the feed and not only in a terminal.

wanted.what: Confirmation of dates from the organisers themselves, rather than from listing sites.
wanted.why_it_matters: Every record here rests on a public listing. The source says so about itself. The twin can carry that honestly, but a calendar the island relies on needs one more hop.
wanted.how_small_it_could_start: The two events the atlas marks as a date to confirm are the whole of the first ask.
